`-writeBufferSizeMB` bounds the per-mount chunk write buffer (memory + swap), not the LevelDB meta cache. The `no space left on device` errors on `/tmp/87a692cf/meta` are the meta-cache LevelDB filling up as the mount caches metadata for the files rclone walks.

Pass `-cacheDir=/some/large/disk` to `weed mount` — that moves both the chunk read cache and the meta cache off `/tmp`. `/tmp` is too small for a 200TB sync with this many files.

The `unsynchronized dir` warnings are separate and benign — they trigger a refresh from the filer.

This is my configuration issue. I adjusted concurrentWriters in weed mount from 1024 to 64, and set the number of checkers for rclone copy to 8. Then, the weed mount log successfully imported a directory with about 40 million small files.

When concurrentWriters is set to 1024, it consumes too many system resources when dealing with a large number of small files, leading to resource contention and potentially causing the system to freeze.
